profiles.summary: Mainnet is listed at v0.16.5 while every public endpoint answers Monad/0.16.7. Between those tags the interpreter's stack pointer was rewritten (StackTop), the 256 bit countl_zero helper was rewritten, and the x86 emitter changed in four places that cycle 12 did not list: memory bounds checks cached per offset element, block-exit stack writes, MSTORE8 from a stack slot and CLZ. All were read and found equivalent, and every opcode and script set was rerun on the 0.16.7 interpreter without a difference.

deltas.delta: Interpreter refactor between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7: the stack is passed as StackTop, a one-past pointer whose index 0 is the top word, instead of a pointer to the top word. instruction_table.hpp changes only signatures and the DUP and SWAP bodies, stack.hpp push, pop and the size computation, call_runtime.hpp the argument pointers, execute.cpp the initial pointer. Every changed expression addresses the same word as before.

deltas.delta: v0.16.6 release notes list three emitter changes for the compiled path in addition to the constant-by-variable shift: memory bounds checked once per offset stack element (PR 2667), block-exit stack writes independent of heap addresses (PR 2644, 2660), and a branchless CLZ. v0.16.5 widened the JUMPDEST scan index to 64 bit (PR 2553).

eth_call at v0.16.7 runs on its own VM constructed InterpreterOnly, separate from the block execution VM; a node with a cold varcode cache compiles a contract synchronously on its first block execution.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transient storage or transaction boundaries. The delayed merkle root rule gives a new reason to trust mined state on the 0.16.7 fleet: a node whose execution of block N-3 differs falls out of consensus at block N.

deltas.delta: Every block proposal carries the state root of block N-3 and a node whose execution differs falls out of consensus and re-executes. The 0.16.7 RPC node was at the finalized tip on 2026-11-24, so its block execution, compiled code included, reproduced the state that the validator set agreed on.

findings.title: MegaETH orders transactions by time in 10 millisecond mini-blocks and skips every candidate once a block has 1,000 new state entries, so a queue of filling transactions delays later ones by its length if skipped transactions keep their place
findings.difference: MegaETH skips every candidate transaction of a block once the block has reached 1,000 new state entries, and orders by arrival inside 10 ms mini-blocks. Ethereum has no per block cap on new state and orders by fee.
findings.mechanism: Unchanged from cycle 4 and 7: one transaction that creates 1,000 new state entries costs about 22.6 million gas, about 0.0000226 ETH at the floor base fee, and after it BlockLimiter::pre_execution_check skips every later candidate of that block, a modifyLiquidity or take included. What this cycle adds is that the deciding link is still open at the newest release: the block executor of v1.7.4 returns a rejected transaction to its caller with the comment that it is typically put back in the pool, the specification says only that it may be reconsidered in a later block, and the code that orders the pool is the closed sequencer. If skipped transactions keep their place ahead of later arrivals, N filling transactions sent from several accounts close N consecutive one second blocks for every transaction that arrived after them. If they go to the back of the pool, the delay is one block per filling transaction that arrives before the victim's.
findings.impact: No funds move. Liquidity removals, swaps and claims are delayed for as long as the sender pays, at about 1.95 ETH per day for one filling transaction per block.
findings.preconditions: The base fee stays near its floor, the sequencer keeps skipped transactions ahead of later arrivals (not confirmed), and the sequencer does not filter the sender.
findings.mitigations: Exits under load can go through an L1 deposit of at most 1,000,000 gas. The operator can price state growth in minimum-size buckets, raise the block limit above the transaction limit, or filter pool entries with large state growth.

cleared.check: Rerun of pmdiff.py (250 scripts) and pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) with the deployed PoolManager bytecode against Ethereum, and pmdiff_explain.py at 150 million gas for Monad.
cleared.result: MegaETH identical on 250 of 250 and 300 of 300. Monad identical on 229 of 250 and 280 of 300; the differing script ids are exactly the ones recorded in opcodes/pmdiff.json and opcodes/pmdiff2.json under the gas limit, the first differing call is a heavy swap that fails with empty return data (16) or a script that ran out of gas as a whole (5), and with 150 million gas 14 of the 21 become identical to Ethereum's record; the rest are scripts that Ethereum's own endpoint cannot finish at 25 million gas plus one request refused with HTTP 429. So the 0.16.7 interpreter gives the same bytes as before on every script that both sides can afford.

cleared.check: Rerun of swaps.py and replay.py: mined Swap events of the deployed PoolManagers against getTickAtSqrtPrice (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:123-236) and the single-step relations of SwapMath.computeSwapStep (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol), multi-step swaps replayed through Pool.swap from storage.
cleared.result: Monad 3,181 swaps and MegaETH 5,913 swaps, all pass the tick relation; of the paired ones 3,085 of 3,092 and 5,444 of 5,588 fit a single step exactly, and all 68 multi-step or other swaps sampled (Monad 7, MegaETH 61) replay to the unit.

cleared.check: Monad interpreter refactor from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 (StackTop one-past stack pointer): DUPn, SWAPn, push, pop, pop_for_overwrite, top_two, check_requirements stack size, call_runtime argument pointers and result slot, the runtime context stack pointer and size, and the initial pointer in execute.cpp.
cleared.result: Old code held a pointer to the top word with the empty stack at bottom minus one; new code holds a pointer one past the top with operator[](i) = *(ptr + i - 1). Old *(top - N) equals new top[-N], old top + 1 equals new next_slot(), old top - bottom equals new next_slot() - bottom (bottom moved by one with the pointer), so every changed expression names the same word. A new vector set, stackedge.py, runs DUPn and SWAPn for n = 1 to 16 at the needed depth and one short, pushes to depths 1,014 to 1,025 followed by DUP1, DUP16 and SWAP16, and memory, hashing and copy runtime calls at stack depth 0 to 1,019: 117 of 117 cases equal the model and Ethereum on Monad and on MegaETH, failures included. The PoolManager uses DUP and SWAP up to 16 in every function, so this is the path every eth_call on the 0.16.7 fleet takes.

cleared.check: Monad countl_zero of category/core/runtime/uint256.hpp, rewritten between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 to a loop without early exit; bit_width uses it, and the emitter uses bit_width for MULMOD with a power of two modulus (modop_optimized) and for EXP with a power of two base.
cleared.result: The new loop keeps the value from the most significant nonzero word: 192 - 64 i + clz(word i), and 256 for zero. A transcription agrees with 256 minus the bit length on 200,007 inputs that include every word boundary. The interpreter uses it only for CLZ (opcode 0x1e), which the PoolManager bytecode does not contain; the compiled MULMOD by 2^96 and 2^128 sites of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 reach it through bit_width at compile time only.

cleared.check: Correction and extension of the cycle 12 clearance that the only emitter change from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 is the constant-by-variable shift. Four more compiled-path changes exist. (1) touch_memory, used by every compiled MLOAD and MSTORE with a non-literal offset, skips the bounds and expansion check when the same stack element already passed it for at least the same size.
cleared.result: Safe as read. The size is recorded on the StackElem object (virtual_stack.hpp lines 216-227 and 279). Every StackElem is constructed fresh by placement new with touched_memory_size_ zero (rc_ptr.hpp line 64, virtual_stack.cpp lines 90-94 and 346-361), and every operation that produces a new value returns a new element: release_general_reg, release_avx_reg and alloc_or_release_* move the register into a new_stack_elem (virtual_stack.cpp lines 821-856, emitter.cpp lines 1161-1233); operations that return an input unchanged (x - 0, x & ~0, shift by 0) return the same value. A cached element therefore always holds the value that was checked, memory never shrinks within a frame, and the data pointer is reloaded from the context on each access, so a reallocation by expansion is followed. Literal offsets, such as mload(0) in src/types/Currency.sol:68, are never cached. The cached path is taken for example by mstore(fmp, 0) at src/types/Currency.sol:77 after mstore(fmp, selector) at line 60.

cleared.check: (2) Monad v0.16.7 write_to_final_stack_offsets, which writes the virtual stack back at the end of every compiled basic block: dependency counts moved from an unordered_map keyed by heap address to an array indexed by each element's lowest stack index, elements are visited in stack index order, and stack words that were stored from general registers are loaded word by word into an AVX register (mov_words_to_ymm).
cleared.result: The algorithm is the same topological write with cycle breaking; only the order in which dependency-free elements are taken changes, and the result does not depend on that order. blockexit.py models the code as written on 200,000 random block-exit states (elements in any mix of stack slot, general register, AVX register and literal, one to three stack indices each): both the stack index order and a shuffled order standing for v0.16.5 leave every final stack index with its element's value, and a planted fault that ignores dependencies is caught in 9,479 of 20,000 cases. mov_words_to_ymm puts word 0 and 1 in the low half and 2 and 3 in the high half, matching the little endian slot layout of stack_offset_to_mem256 (emitter.cpp lines 109-116). The scratch register it uses is free at allocation and distinct from the init register and from every element register. The array index stays in range under the invariant v0.16.5 already needed (an element at a slot in [min_delta, top] has its lowest index there). Every JUMP and JUMPI of the PoolManager, among them the TickBitmap and BitMath branches, passes through this code.

cleared.check: (3) Monad v0.16.7 block_prologue stack bound check, changed from 'min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024' to 'max_delta - min_delta > 1024' before the two runtime checks, and (4) MSTORE8 of a value held in a stack slot and the branchless CLZ.
cleared.result: With min_delta at most 0 and max_delta at least 0, every block the new static test rejects is one whose two runtime checks (size at least -min_delta and size at most 1024 - max_delta) no stack size passes, and the old static test is implied by the new one, so both versions fail exactly the same stack sizes and an exceptional halt consumes all gas either way. MSTORE8 now reads four bytes of the little endian slot and stores the low byte, the same byte as before. The PoolManager bytecode has no MSTORE8 (0x53) and no CLZ (0x1e) by linear disassembly of build/PoolManager.json.

cleared.check: Whether code compiled by the 0.16.7 emitter on the RPC fleet could compute PoolManager state that differs from the validators, who are listed on v0.16.5, without anyone noticing.
cleared.result: No. Every node executes every block and checks the state root that consensus carries D = 3 blocks later; a node whose execution differs falls out of consensus. rpc.monad.xyz reported Monad/0.16.7 and stood at the finalized tip (block 125,067,658) on 2026-11-24, so its block execution agrees with the validators' state on every block it has executed. This covers storage, balances and nonces, not logs or receipts.

cleared.check: Lead L-674: does eth_call on Monad share the block execution VM, and what happens on a node with a cold varcode cache.
cleared.result: eth_call uses a separate member vm::VM vm_{vm::VM::InterpreterOnly} of the RPC executor, with the comment that the compiler would misreport out-of-gas as generic failure, so no eth_call can reach compiled code on any node. Block execution with a cold cache calls cached_compile_and_execute_raw, compiling synchronously on the first call; with a warm cache it interprets and starts asynchronous compilation once interpretation of the code hash has used max_code_size(10,240, size) gas. The earlier statement that eth_call tests only the interpreter stands.

leads.question: Which share of Monad validators runs v0.16.7 (with the PR 2667 memory check cache and the new block-exit writes) rather than the listed v0.16.5, and does any validator run v0.16.6?
leads.why: The new compiled paths were cleared by reading and by a model; the delayed merkle root means a fault in them would split the network rather than silently move funds, which makes the split itself the hazard to rule out before an upgrade.

leads.question: Which Rust toolchain built mega-reth v2.2.3-72527bc and the sequencer, and does any revm 40.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3 or ruint 1.19.0 function call a closure through Fn::call or call_mut with a by-pointer argument that the closure mutates, the shape of rust-lang/rust issue 155241?
leads.why: mega-evm itself left the affected nightly in v1.7.3; a binary built with an affected toolchain could compute a wrong result on a path no eth_call of the replica would show if the replica was built differently.

leadResults.answer: The mainnet page names v0.16.5 / MONAD_TEN as current and the release page lists v0.16.7 for testnet only, while every public endpoint reports Monad/0.16.7 and is at the finalized tip, so at least the RPC fleet runs 0.16.7 on mainnet and agrees with the validators' state roots. Whether the PoolManager is compiled cannot be read from mined gas: compiled and interpreted execution must charge identical gas or the state root would differ (the emitter adds the remaining static gas back for GAS and every runtime call, emitter.cpp lines 3106-3116), so receipts are the same either way and the proposed method cannot answer it.

The size estimate still needs a build of the asmjit emitter, which was not done (no forge or compiler install allowed beyond what is present; the Monad tree is C++ and was not built). Unchanged since cycle 12: bound 778,528 bytes, of which 96,036 are the jump table.

eth_call uses its own InterpreterOnly VM at v0.16.7 (monad_executor.cpp 1306-1309) and never reaches compiled code. Block execution on a cold varcode cache compiles synchronously on the first call (vm.cpp 167-172), so a restarted node runs the PoolManager compiled from its first block execution if the size bound allows.

Mainnet version per docs: v0.16.5. Endpoints: 0.16.7. The compile decision code (vm.cpp, x86.hpp) is byte identical in both, so the answer to whether the PoolManager is compiled is the same on both releases and still depends on the asmjit size estimate (L-672).
mega-reth v2.2.3 is closed and still the version the replica reports; its keccak cache configuration cannot be read. Operator level only.

Answered by cycle 12 theme-mined-liquidity-2: with pool keys taken from the recorded call frames, 276 of the 277 Monad transactions, the 42 without a PositionManager key among them, were rerun and match to the unit; one is left aside for a missing key.

At mega-evm v1.7.4 the executor still hands a rejected transaction back to the caller (executor.rs 586-596, identical to v1.7.3) and the specification says only that a skipped transaction may be reconsidered in a later block. The ordering code is the closed sequencer and no block with a full state growth budget was observed, so the place a skipped transaction takes in the pool is still unconfirmed. F-062 stays low and is re-reported with that statement.

The stateless validator was not built or run: it needs the mega-evm source tree and a crate fetch that this session cannot do from a clone. No new public party publishing validator results was found. The receipt and storage comparisons of cycles 10 to 12 remain the evidence.
